questions.problem:
The displacement (in centimeters) of an ant moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)={t}^{2}+3t,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds.
Find the ant's acceleration at $t=10$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+3t) \\  & =2t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+3) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration at time $t=10,$ we substitute this into the above:

$$
a(10)=2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration when $t=10$ seconds is $2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

questions.problem:
The velocity $v$ (in $\text{m/s}$) of a particle at time $t$ (in seconds) is given by $v(t)={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t+1.$ Calculate the velocity of the particle when the acceleration $a$ is equal to $2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t>0.$

When $a=2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ the velocity is $v=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate $v(t)$ to calculate $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t+1) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-6t+2\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the time when the acceleration is $a=2,$ we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =3{t}^{2}-6t+2 \\ 0 & =3{t}^{2}-6t \\ 3t(t-2) & =0 \\ t & =0,2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $t=2$ since $t>0.$

Then, to calculate the velocity at time $t=2,$ we substitute this into the equation for the velocity:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =(2)^{3}-3(2)^{2}+2(2)+1 \\  & =8-12+4+1 \\  & =1\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity when $a=2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ is $v=1\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle at a Particular Moment Given Its Position
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+\frac{6}{t+2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+6(t+2)^{-1}) \\  & =2t-6(t+2)^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-6(t+2)^{-2}) \\  & =2+12(t+2)^{-3} \\  & =2+\frac{12}{(t+2)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$
